title: Project Test Strategy and Risk-Based Verification
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Project Test Strategy and Risk-Based Verification.
Apply project test strategy and risk-based verification to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to project test strategy and risk-based verification.
Review common mistakes and risks in project test strategy and risk-based verification.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using project test strategy and risk-based verification principles.

understand.concept: A test strategy decides what to verify, at which level and with what evidence. Unit tests focus on small units, integration tests check collaboration, and end-to-end tests exercise workflows. Risk-based testing prioritizes likely and high-impact failures.
understand.whyItMatters: A deliberate strategy finds defects efficiently and avoids low-value tests.
understand.analogy: A building inspection checks materials, connected systems and the completed structure at different levels.
understand.analogyLimit: Tests provide evidence for selected scenarios; they cannot prove the absence of every defect.
understand.summary: Project Test Strategy and Risk-Based Verification helps learners plan and deliver maintainable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Start with critical workflows and business invariants. Test domain functions with unit tests, repositories and adapters with integration tests, and a small set of journeys end to end. Include normal, boundary and failure cases. Keep tests deterministic.

examples.title: Deterministic test

print(total(12, 3) == 36)
